posts.title: English - Christine Rice and Jacques Imbrailo Stand Out in Iphigénie en Tauride at the London Coliseum
posts.description: Iphigénie en Tauride of 1779 was Christoph Willibald Gluck ’s fifth and penultimate opera for the French stage. In it he took his ideas concerning reform opera to what might be deemed their logical conclusion, employing récitatif accompagné and largely omitting the dance movements that were a hallmark of French tragédie en musique . Knowing that many of the operas and ballets he had already written in Italian would probably never be performed again, he also recycled a substantial number of compositions from them as a way of keeping the music alive. Nicolas-François Guillard’s libretto was based primarily on Claude Guimond de la Touche’s spoken tragedy of 1757, whose ultimate source was Euripides’ Iphigenia in Tauris . In direct contrast to Aeschylus’ telling of the wider tale, Iphigénie was not killed on Aulis by her father Agamemnon because, as he was about to sacrifice her, the goddess Artemis replaced her on the altar with a deer, and swept her off to the land of the Taurians. posts.title: English - Liceu: I Capuleti e i Montecchi. Oropesa and Lupinacci Make a Great Work of an Imperfect Opera
posts.description: An opera does not have to apologise for not being a Shakespearean tragedy. Vincenzo Bellini ’s I Capuleti e i Montecchi shares its protagonists and tragic ending with the English playwright’s drama, but belongs to an earlier Italian tradition that had already shaped the story of the two lovers. It is not an adaptation of Shakespeare that should be judged by its fidelity to the original, but another way of telling a story that has taken many forms. To compare the two as though the opera had to compete with Shakespeare’s tragedy is to start on the wrong foot. The circumstances in which the opera was composed help explain the unevenness of its score. Bellini had little more than a month to prepare the work for the 1830 Carnival season in Venice, and reused a considerable amount of music from Zaira , which had failed the previous year. posts.title: English - Annilese Miskimmon’s New Production of Tosca for English National Opera at the London Coliseum
posts.description: Based on Victorien Sardou’s 1887 French-language play, Giacomo Puccini ’s Tosca of 1900, with a libretto by Luigi Illica and Giuseppe Giacosa, not only occurs in a specific time and place, but on a precise date that can be linked to an historical event. All of the action takes place during the afternoon, evening and early morning of 17 and 18 June 1800, following the Battle of Marengo between Napoleon’s army and Austrian forces. The Austrians were initially triumphant and sent news of victory back to Rome, but the city’s celebrations were cut short when a later report revealed that Napoleon subsequently mustered reinforcements and actually inflicted a crushing defeat. Tosca is set across the hours when the contradictory messages arrive in Rome. Angelotti, a consul of the city when it was a republic but a prisoner since Neapolitan forces began to occupy it, escapes from the Castel Sant’Angelo and turns to the painter Cavaradossi to hide him.
